target.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR1/5 in the durable-core stack. It is docs/RFC only: it proposes a narrow residual-gap durable-core boundary and proof plan for reviewer discussion before any implementation PR claims runtime behavior.

This PR does not publish a release architecture contract. It does not claim shipped runtime behavior, wake replay, CLI/Gateway controls, session handoff, external transport delivery, schema migration, or product retry/resume policy.

## Scope updated 2026-07-15

- Reframes the architecture page as **Durable Core Residual-Gap Architecture Proposal**.
- Reframes the proof page as **Durable Core Residual-Gap Compatibility Check Plan**.
- Renames the durable proposal doc slugs from retired prerelease names to proposal slugs:
  - `/specs/durable-core-proposal-architecture`
  - `/specs/durable-core-proposal-test-plan`
- Aligns generated route inventory (`docs/docs_map.md`) and the zh-CN glossary with those final titles/routes; `docs/docs.json` intentionally does not expose the proposal pages in public navigation.
- Explicitly positions the RFC as complementary to existing TaskFlow/database-first ownership, not a competing shipped persistence contract.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can accept long-running work, delegate it to subagents, defer it through waits, route it through channels, and recover after restarts. Existing owners already persist important state. The remaining proposal is about residual cross-owner invariants: stable work refs, auditable events, owner/lease expiry, terminal immutability, wake/attention routing, delivery evidence boundaries, inspection, and fail-closed recovery.

## Non-scope

- No runtime behavior.
- No database/schema migration.
- No CLI/Gateway controls.
- No worker loop or wake replay implementation.
- No plugin/channel delivery behavior.
- No Task Flow or Workboard product feature implementation.
- No claim that external transport delivery is covered by internal session handoff.

## Evidence

### 2026-07-15 authored evidence for exact head

- Problem statement: reviewers need a public, non-runtime RFC artifact that names the residual durable-core invariants without presenting them as shipped release behavior or an approved public contract.
- Authored validation evidence: exact-head local docs validation and GitHub CI are listed below; the latest patch removes the proposal pages from public Technical Reference navigation so unapproved architecture is not published as endorsed reference material.
- Runtime evidence boundary: this PR is documentation/glossary plus non-navigation generated route inventory only, so real-behavior proof is not applicable beyond the absence of runtime/schema/transport changes and docs-focused validation. No live gateway, worker, or transport behavior is changed by this PR.

## Current head and proof

### 2026-07-15 exact-head proof update

- Current PR head: `080e9a8ee5ebd0d5597bc95a52e03b453ecdbb85`
- Base branch: `release/2026.7.1`
- Diff surface: docs/spec proposal pages, zh-CN glossary, and generated route inventory only; `docs/docs.json` has no proposal-page navigation entries.
- Re-review requested: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107375#issuecomment-4979446974

| Gate | Command/Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Docs map | `pnpm docs:map:check` | passed locally on exact head |
| Targeted MDX/docs JSON | `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/specs/durable-core-proposal-architecture.md docs/specs/durable-core-proposal-test-plan.md docs/docs.json` | passed locally on exact head |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check HEAD` | passed locally on exact head |
| GitHub CI docs | `CI / check-docs` | passed on exact head |
| GitHub CI security/preflight | `CI / preflight`, `CI / security-fast`, dependency and security guards | passed on exact head |
| Real behavior proof | GitHub `Real behavior proof` check | not applicable to this docs-only RFC; the PR body and proof comment keep the change scoped away from runtime/schema/transport behavior |

The previous proof for `f9d3698ed9b614fd9107883d47c4c1dbc80b2b18` is superseded by this exact-head update. `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` remains blocked by unrelated branch-base glossary omissions outside this PR1 durable-core surface.

## ClawSweeper concerns addressed

- Release-specific contract: removed/reframed as an RFC proposal and residual-gap boundary.
- Stale prerelease route wording: removed from the proposal doc slugs.
- Page/glossary mismatch: glossary source strings now match the final durable-core page titles.
- Ownership overlap: the docs now explicitly build on TaskFlow/database-first owners and describe only residual cross-owner contracts.

## Remaining review risk

A durable-work owner or maintainer still needs to decide whether this residual-gap boundary is the right upstream architecture direction. This PR only makes the proposal reviewable; it does not implement or assert the behavior.
